Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Dr. Nina Khalil, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech had a productive third quarter, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance: our overall performance highlights and key achievements; organic revenue growth by segment and geography; FDA approvals and CE marks obtained; gross margin trends and supply chain commentary; inventory management and working capital optimization; and revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and full year.

Jordan will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Khalil will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our overall performance highlights and key achievements.

This quarter exemplifies our ability to deliver above-market growth, margin leverage, and shareholder returns in a competitive landscape. Worldwide revenue reached a record $2.85 billion, up 13% on a reported basis and 11% organically—our strongest Q3 organic growth in five years. This was fueled by procedural volume tailwinds, market share gains, and the successful ramp of our innovation pipeline. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.52, a 17% increase year-over-year, beating our guidance midpoint by $0.07, thanks to 280 basis points of operating margin expansion to 28.5%. Free cash flow was exceptional at $950 million, up 22%, enabling $1.2 billion in share repurchases and dividends year-to-date.

Breaking it down by franchise—a core strength of our diversified model—Cardiovascular revenue surged 16% organically to $1.1 billion, outpacing the broader market. Structural heart was the star, with transcatheter aortic valve replacement, or TAVR, procedures up 22% globally, driven by our next-gen EvoQ valve, which captured two points of U.S. market share from competitors' platforms. Left atrial appendage closure devices like our Watchman FLX grew 19%, benefiting from expanded guidelines and our direct-to-consumer awareness campaigns. In ablation therapies, our Volt pulsed-field ablation system—cleared by the FDA just 12 months ago—drove 25% growth, with over 15,000 procedures worldwide, positioning us ahead in paroxysmal AFib.

MedSurg and Neuromodulation delivered 9% organic growth to $850 million. Orthopedics implantables rose 11%, with our Trinity porous titanium hip systems seeing double-digit adoption in revision surgeries, gaining share in the $8 billion U.S. market. Endoscopy hit a milestone with 14% growth, propelled by our single-use duodenoscopes, which addressed infection control concerns and boosted U.S. procedural volumes by 18%. Neuromodulation was up 12%, led by our Infinity DBS system for Parkinson's, where adaptive deep brain stimulation algorithms reduced battery depletion by 30%—a key differentiator in our 250-plus clinical sites.

Diabetes and Diagnostics grew 10% to $500 million, with our continuous glucose monitoring FreeStyle Libre 3 sensor achieving 28% U.S. growth, now serving 4.5 million patients through superior seven-day wear time and smartphone integration. Our AI-powered imaging diagnostics, like the EchoAI platform for echocardiography, launched in EMEA and generated $120 million in initial pull-through revenue.

On the technical initiatives front, R&D investment hit 12.5% of sales at $355 million, yielding three FDA approvals this quarter alone: the EvoQ TAVR for low-risk patients, Volt PFA for persistent AFib, and our Magnebot robotic platform for spinal fusions, which reduces OR time by 25% compared to other systems in ortho applications. We're also advancing our digital health ecosystem—40% of our devices now connect via our CloudMed platform, enabling predictive analytics that cut readmissions by 15% in partnered ACOs.

Regionally, performance was balanced yet opportunistic. The U.S., 60% of revenue, grew 14% organically, supported by favorable reimbursement under the CY2025 IPPS final rule, which preserved pass-through status for 15 of our devices. EMEA was up 9% constant currency, with strong TAVR penetration in Germany and Italy amid aging demographics—EU28 TAVR volumes rose 16%. APAC accelerated to 18% organic growth, led by China at 25% despite NRDL pricing pressures; our joint venture expanded access to 500 Tier-3 hospitals. Emerging markets like LATAM contributed 12% growth via distributor expansions in Brazil for orthopedics.

Key achievements this quarter include closing our $4.2 billion acquisition of NeuroStim Inc., adding a pipeline of non-invasive VNS therapies for epilepsy that projects $300 million in revenue synergies by FY2026. We also secured a $1.5 billion sole-source agreement with Kaiser Permanente for bundled CGM and insulin delivery systems, and surpassed 50% market share in U.S. pulsed-field ablation. Sustainability-wise, 75% of our manufacturing is now carbon-neutral, aligning with EU MDR requirements and enhancing our ESG score.

These results affirm our 'Innovate, Penetrate, Expand' framework. We're capitalizing on secular tailwinds: a 4.5% CAGR in global procedural volumes through 2030, minimally invasive shifts, and AI/ML integration—areas where we invest 20% more in R&D than peers. Market share expanded 100 basis points overall.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

We delivered another quarter of robust organic revenue growth, up 12% year-over-year on an organic basis, excluding the impacts of our recent acquisition of NeuroVasc Solutions and unfavorable foreign exchange headwinds of about two percentage points. This performance underscores the strength of our core franchises amid a recovering elective procedure environment and our disciplined execution on innovation and market share gains.

By segment, we saw broad-based growth across all major categories, driven by higher procedural volumes, favorable reimbursement dynamics in key markets, and the ramp-up of our next-generation product portfolio.

Cardiovascular Segment grew 15% organically, our largest segment at 38% of total revenue, posting double-digit growth for the seventh straight quarter. This was fueled by a 22% surge in TAVR volumes in the US, where we gained 180 basis points of market share to 28%, thanks to the full US launch of our EvoFlow Pro valve platform, which features enhanced paravalvular leak reduction and 20% faster deployment times. In structural heart, our FlexRepair XT transcatheter mitral repair system contributed significantly, up 30%, as we expanded into Asia-Pacific with IDEAL study data supporting broader indications. Globally, coronary intervention revenues grew 11%, bolstered by our drug-eluting stents amid stabilizing PCI volumes.

Orthopedics Segment grew 10% organically at 25% of revenues, with hips and knees up 13% on 8% higher unit volumes. The star was our Cementless Trinity hip system, which captured 15% US market share in primary hips, driven by superior 10-year survivorship data from our PROSPECT registry. Revision business grew 7%, resilient despite softer hospital capital budgets, as we leaned into our robotic-assisted smart knee with integrated AI-driven kinematics analysis for personalized implant planning—early adopter sites are reporting 25% reduction in post-op complications.

MedSurg and Endoscopy Segment grew 9% organically, this 22% slice led by a 14% jump in endoscopy on the global rollout of our single-use VizScope HD flexible endoscopes, which address CRE infection risks and have secured GPO contracts covering 40% of US beds. Hernia repair meshes, enhanced with bioresorbable coatings to minimize chronic pain, added meaningfully, up 12%, as we navigated reimbursement headwinds in Europe by partnering with local payers on value-based bundles. Soft tissue repair was up 6% YoY.

Diagnostics and Monitoring Segment grew 11% organically at 15% of revenues, benefiting from our CGM expansion, with the LibreSync Pro patch sensor generating strong growth as we hit 4 million US patients on therapy through aggressive DTC marketing and Apple Health interoperability. Remote patient monitoring via our VitalHub platform surged on post-COVID telehealth tailwinds, with AI algorithms predicting 85% of arrhythmia events pre-hospitalization, securing CMS reimbursement parity.

Shifting to geography, our organic growth profile reflects both mature market resilience and emerging market acceleration.

United States grew 14% organically, 62% of revenues, driven by 12% procedural volume increases outpacing industry recovery estimates. Medicare Advantage penetration at 52% of eligible patients boosted uptake of our bundled payment models for TAVR and orthopedics, while our direct-to-hospital sales force expansion yielded 250 bps share gains in ambulatory surgery centers.

EMEA grew 8% organically, 18% of revenues, tempered by FX drag but lifted by 15% expansion in Germany and the Nordics on IFU expansions for our EvoFlow valve under EU MDR. UK NHS tenders for endoscopy single-use devices added significantly, though Italian reimbursement delays capped potential—we're addressing this via EU HTA engagement.

APAC grew 16% organically, 14% of revenues, with China up 22% on NMPA approvals for FlexRepair XT and Trinity hips, capturing 12% share in a fast-growing market. Japan volumes rose 14% post-reimbursement for CGM, while India and ASEAN pilots for low-cost orthopedics drove 25% growth in emerging pockets. Supply chain localization in Singapore mitigated tariff risks.

Rest of World grew 7% organically, 6% of revenues, with Brazil's elective rebound adding tailwinds to cardio and ortho.

These results validate our framework: We've invested heavily in R&D, yielding a high new product contribution to growth. Margins expanded thanks to manufacturing efficiencies and pricing discipline amid GLP-1 headwinds that we see as neutral long-term. Looking forward, we're well-positioned to outperform peers, leveraging our procedural growth multiple.

Moving on to FDA approvals and CE marks obtained.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, I want to highlight our regulatory momentum, which is transformative. We secured four FDA approvals and three CE marks across our core franchises in cardiovascular, orthopedics, and diagnostics—our strongest pipeline quarter in years. This unlocks $2.8 billion in addressable market opportunity over the next three years, with projected revenue contributions ramping to 15-20% of our top-line growth by FY2025.

First, our flagship cardiovascular win: FDA Premarket Approval for the VantageFlex Drug-Eluting Stent. This is a game-changer in the coronary intervention space, a $7.5 billion global market growing at 6.8% CAGR through 2030 driven by rising PCI volumes. VantageFlex features our proprietary bioresorbable polymer matrix—reducing late stent thrombosis by 42% in our pivotal ORBIT-3 trial versus predicate devices—paired with next-gen everolimus elution. The PMA path was rigorous: we leveraged Breakthrough Device Designation, shaving 18 months off the timeline, with our IDE study showing 97.2% acute success and 8.9% target lesion failure at 12 months.

This catapults us into the US DES market, where we'll capture 12-15% share within 24 months through our cath lab footprint. In Europe, we obtained CE Mark under MDR Class III—the first DES approved post the 2021 overhaul—positioning us ahead of competitors, with early EU tenders showing 25% pricing premium uptake.

Second, FDA 510(k) clearance for our OrthoGuide Robotic-Assisted Navigation System. Orthopedics robotics is exploding to $15 billion by 2028 at 18% CAGR. OrthoGuide integrates AI-driven haptic feedback and intraoperative CT fusion, reducing revision rates by 31% versus benchmarks. Clearance was at 147 days, beating FDA medians. This expands into spines, targeting $1.2 billion US opportunity. CE Mark under MDR Class IIb followed.

Third, FDA De Novo classification for EchoAI Diagnostic Ultrasound Platform. In the $9.2 billion POCUS TAM, EchoAI achieves 94.5% sensitivity for automated scoring. De Novo granted Class II status; CE Mark under IVDR Class C came concurrently.

Fourth, FDA PMA supplement for expanded NeuroFlow Intracranial Stent Retriever indications, adding LVO stroke thrombectomy in a $1.1 billion market, with 87% recanalization rates.

These wins reflect our Regulatory Velocity Initiative, investing in digital twins and RWE, cutting cycles by 28%. We're ahead of industry headwinds with 100% first-cycle approvals. Financially, expect Q4 revenue lift and margin expansion. Our 12-product 2024 pipeline positions us for 22% organic growth.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

Our non-GAAP gross margin came in at 68.7% for the quarter, up 250 basis points year-over-year and 110 basis points sequentially. This marks our third consecutive quarter of expansion and puts us on track for our full-year guidance midpoint.

Favorable product mix contributed 160 basis points, with accelerated adoption of higher-margin structural heart like the Evolut PRO+ TAVR valve, up 28% and now 22% of Cardiovascular revenue. In Robotics, our Hugo RAS system ramped, driving mix shift with ASPs at $1.4 million per unit.

Cost headwinds shaved 90 basis points from raw material inflation in resins and polycarbonate, up 12% YoY, and electronics like silicon carbide chips. FX was a 20 basis point tailwind. Pricing added 80 basis points through increases on Diabetes products, with net price realization at 102.5% of list via value-based contracts.

Regionally, US margins hit 71.2%, fueled by reimbursement tailwinds; Europe at 65.4% due to MDR costs, now 92% certified; APAC at 67.8%, up 300 bps on approvals.

We expect Q4 expansion to 69.5-70%. Supply chain resilience improved to 94% on-time delivery, inventory at 142 days. Semiconductor allocation eased with secondary sources; resins locked via contracts. Vertical integration in Ireland cuts outsourcing; 3D-printed implants reduce lead times. AI predictive analytics flagged disruptions. Nearshoring to Mexico, localization in China and Singapore de-risk. Targeting 72% margins by FY2027 via premiumization, automation, and sustainability procurement. Risks like labor inflation are buffered.

Then, inventory management and working capital optimization.

Our Days Inventory Outstanding improved to 82 days, down from 95 a year ago, with turnover at 4.5x above industry median. Cash Conversion Cycle compressed 18 days to 65 days, freeing $165 million in cash redeployed to R&D and repurchases. Working capital as % of revenue dropped to 18%, top quartile.

Drivers include AI-powered demand sensing reducing forecast error 22%; Vendor-Managed Inventory covering 35% of raw materials, boosting DPO 8 days; RFID and ABC classification slashing discrepancies and obsolescence by $12 million.

US DIO at 78 days via consignment; EMEA at 88 days with localized manufacturing; APAC at 92 days stabilized by JIT. Piloting blockchain for biologics, targeting 10% further DIO cut. This generates superior FCF, fueling innovation.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and full year.

Our outlook reflects continued momentum across cardiovascular rhythm management, structural heart, orthopedics, and robotics and endoscopy. It incorporates strong procedural recovery, with U.S. elective volumes 8% above pre-COVID, and market share gains in TAVR and robotic surgery.

For Q4, total revenue of $4.15 to $4.25 billion, 9% to 12% reported growth, 8% to 11% organic, above prior guide, driven by U.S. orthopedics and robotics acceleration.

By segment: Cardiovascular and Structural Heart ~$1.75 billion, 10-12% organic, TAVR tailwind with VitalFlow valve at 28% share, offset by modest ASP pressure; Orthopedics $1.0 billion, 7-9%, Mako-like system penetration >40%; Robotics and Endoscopy $850 million, 18-22%, VitalBot ramp with 25% QoQ placements, 85% utilization; Other $550 million, flat to 2%.

Regionally: U.S. 10-13%, reimbursement support; EMEA 6-8%, robotics strength offset by France; APAC 5-7%, Japan TAVR and China ramps, monitoring macro.

Full year 2024 raised to $16.3 to $16.5 billion, 8-9% organic from $15.1 billion.

Adjusted gross margin 68.5-69.0% in Q4, up 50 bps, from manufacturing efficiencies, mix, supply tailwinds like 10% lower resin costs, offset by R&D amortization. Operating margin 25.5-26.0%, full-year OpEx ~$6.95 billion or 42.5-43% of revenue, R&D 12.5% at $2.0 billion. Full-year gross 68.0-68.5%, operating 24.5-25.0%, tax 16.5%, shares 1.42 billion, $1.5 billion repurchases.

This underscores 'Innovate, Acquire, Optimize': FDA for VitalBot Gen3 Q1 2025, Trinity CRM mid-year; $300 million FY25 CapEx for AI; M&A tuck-ins. Risks: reimbursement, GLP-1 <2% drag, APAC geopolitics; resilience from 85% U.S. manufacturing. Committed to 8-10% growth, 100 bps margin expansion.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan for a review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid financial performance this quarter, aligning with the highlights across segments and geographies. Revenue of $2.85 billion exceeded expectations, with organic growth of 11-12% reflecting the procedural recovery and our market share gains. Expenses were well-controlled, with OpEx at 43% of sales, driving operating margin expansion. Profitability metrics were strong, with adjusted EPS of $1.52 and robust free cash flow supporting capital returns. For the full year, we're on track with raised guidance, and Q4 sets us up for continued momentum, incorporating the details Alex outlined on revenue and margins.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Khalil for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Nina Khalil:
Thank you, Jordan. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for VitalBot Gen3, which is showing promising results in enhancing OR efficiency by 20% via predictive analytics in robotic-assisted surgery. Our pipeline remains robust, with investments in AI-enhanced hemodynamic monitors, bioresorbable stents, and expansions in neuromodulation and structural heart. Recent FDA approvals like VantageFlex and OrthoGuide validate our velocity, and we're advancing 12 products for 2025, including next-gen TAVR valves and pulsed-field ablation systems, positioning us for 22% organic growth contributions.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Dr. Khalil. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one on your telephone. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On organic growth, can you expand on the APAC acceleration, especially China, and how you're navigating NRDL pressures?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. APAC was a standout at 16% organic, with China up 22% on NMPA approvals for FlexRepair XT and Trinity hips, capturing 12% share despite pricing pressures. Our JV with local partners expanded to 500 Tier-3 hospitals, and localization mitigates tariffs. NRDL impacts are manageable through value-based bundles, similar to peers, and we see sustained 18% market growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great results. On gross margins, what gives you confidence in the 69.5-70% Q4 guide amid cost headwinds?

Jordan Lee:
Emily, thanks. Confidence stems from mix favoring high-margin robotics and structural heart, pricing discipline at 102.5% realization, and supply efficiencies—resins down 10%, vertical integration yielding 200 bps. We've stress-tested inflation scenarios with buffers, and regional strength in APAC and US supports the expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Impressive regulatory wins. How does the OrthoGuide clearance impact commercial rollout, and any early traction?

Tom Hargrove:
Mike, OrthoGuide is a big step in robotics, targeting $1.2 billion in spines. Early US launch via 4,200 accounts shows +22% QoQ utilization from upgrades. Co-marketing with partners like Zimmer, projecting $250 million additive by 2026. EU MDR CE Mark enables Q1 2025 Europe ramp, with 31% revision rate reduction driving adoption.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. On inventory optimization, how sustainable is the DIO improvement, and any blockchain pilot updates?

Dr. Nina Khalil:
Lisa, DIO at 82 days is sustainable via AI forecasting—22% error reduction—and VMI at 35%. US consignment with IDNs like Kaiser holds $80 million off-balance. Blockchain pilot for biologics starts Q4, targeting traceability and 10% further cut, enhancing resilience like in recent allograft shortages.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
